label: Content A/B testing
title: Testing individual page elements.
summary: Prepare content variants, choose how impressions are allocated and keep these actions connected.
problem: Once variants are ready, the user needs to decide how they reach the audience. The interface offers three modes: First, AI and Weights.
decision: Each mode reveals its own settings, rather than presenting every traffic control at once.
story: The challenge
The visual editor supports experiments with text, images and combinations of elements. Users need to understand both what they are changing and how each version will be shown to their audience.
The solution

Experiment settings remain inside the editor. The page preview preserves context while the selected element’s properties appear alongside it, connecting content preparation with impression allocation.
Three allocation modes
First keeps the first variant. AI automatically reallocates impressions towards stronger content. Weights provides manual control. The available fields change with the selected mode.
My contribution
I designed the visual landing-page editor, A/B tests for text, images and combinations, and the First, AI and Weights modes. Editor states connect content preparation with experiment settings.
reasoning: Keeping the preview close
A text or image variant makes sense within the page composition. A persistent preview makes changes visible in context without repeatedly switching between settings and viewing.
One pattern across content types
Text Split and Image Split repeat the same control structure. Changing the content type does not require learning a different interaction.
Reveal settings after a choice
First, AI and Weights require different decisions. Conversion and weight fields appear with the relevant mode so that the next step follows the user’s choice.

label: Visits / Recordings
title: See the actions behind a visit.
summary: A session player reveals where a visitor clicked and how they moved through a page.
problem: Visit statistics describe the outcome. Understanding behaviour requires reconstructing the sequence of on-page actions.
decision: Recordings open from the Visits table. The list, player and timeline share one window, with an option to expand the viewing area.
story: The challenge
Help a marketer move from visit metrics to a person’s actual clicks, movement and pauses on a page.
From visit to recording
The entry point is the Visits context menu. The recordings list stays beside the player, so switching sessions does not require returning to the main table.
Control the pace
Pause and ten-second jumps support close inspection. Playback at 1×–4× and Skip inactive help move through periods without activity. The timeline preserves the position within the recording.
Room for analysis
Expanded mode hides the list and enlarges the recording area. Playback controls stay in place so changing the view does not interrupt inspection.
Interface states
Before selection, the player explains where to start. Loading feedback confirms progress, while the highlighted row identifies the current visit.
reasoning: A persistent reference point
The adjacent list preserves the connection between the recording and its visit, allowing sessions to be compared without rebuilding context in the main table.
Two viewing scales
The list supports finding recordings; a larger player supports examining details. Collapsing the list changes the scale while preserving playback controls and position.
Uneven event density
Speed controls and skipping inactivity support both quick review and close inspection. Pause and the timeline keep the user in control.

label: Cohort analytics
title: From an overview to a specific slice.
summary: A cohort table with period selection, individual cells and contextual details.
problem: Compare cohorts over time and inspect details without losing the selected group’s context.
decision: The period controls the scope of the view. A selected cell links the table to its details, while expanded mode creates more room for comparison.
story: Comparison over time
The table combines cohorts and periods in one view. Colour makes differences between values easier to notice.
From overview to detail
A selected cell sets the context for detailed statistics. The user examines a specific slice without losing their position in the table.
Different scales
A short period provides a compact view. A longer period and expanded mode make broader comparisons possible.
Cell states
Colour and selection states connect readability with the current analytical focus.
reasoning: A cell connects overview and detail
An explicit selection identifies the group and period behind the details, giving both views a shared focus.
Scale follows the question
Short periods reveal early changes; longer periods show cohort development. Expanded mode makes room for a wider table without changing selection behaviour.
Patterns and precise reading
Colour helps reveal patterns across values. Selection and details support closer inspection of a particular slice.

summary: Land and Destination variants, First, AI and Weights modes, and metric views.
problem: Define page variants and traffic destinations, select an allocation method and understand each mode’s parameters.
decision: A shared component combines landing variants with conversion selection, manual weights and allocation metrics.
story: What is being compared
A campaign compares pages and traffic destinations. Land defines landing-page variants; Destination defines the visitor’s next step.
Three allocation methods
First uses the first variant. AI follows the selected conversion. Weights gives manual control over the relative weight of each row.
Metrics beside variants
Conversions, clicks and percentage shares remain within the list context, connecting allocation to the pages it affects.
A progressive setup
Empty states prompt variant creation. Types, parameters and metrics appear as the setup progresses, preserving one component structure.
reasoning: Connect variants and impressions
Conversions and manual weights belong to particular page variants. Settings beside the rows make it clear which destination each change affects.

label: Team and permissions
title: Collaboration within an object’s context.
summary: Connect campaigns, people, teams and permissions in one workflow.
problem: Campaign work also involves people: finding participants, choosing teams and checking or changing permissions.
decision: People management stays connected to the object they work on, keeping permissions near the task.
story: The challenge
Manage access within an object’s context: find people or teams, add participants and set permissions.
The solution
The window separates organisation members from people with access. All, Users and Teams tabs, search, bulk addition and drag-and-drop form one flow.
Clear states
No search results, no teams and an exhausted list of available users need different explanations. Specific messages clarify the situation and the available next action.
Access control
Permissions can be edited for individuals and teams. Contextual actions reflect the owner’s or another administrator’s role.
reasoning: Explain why a list is empty

label: Registration
title: An introduction, one step at a time.
summary: Guide someone from an invitation to a workspace, revealing settings progressively.
problem: Before advertising work can begin, a new user needs to accept an invitation, enter their details and set up a workspace.
decision: Attention stays on the current action. Other settings are introduced in the following steps.
story: The challenge
First entry involves an invitation, personal details, security, a workspace and a subscription. These need a sequence that does not require every setting at once.
The solution
Registration is divided into states with one current action. Two-factor authentication can be configured between steps, and subscription selection can be skipped.
My contribution
I designed registration and the associated first-entry states, progressively introducing profile details, security and workspace settings.
reasoning: Introduce complexity gradually
Profile, security and workspace settings solve different tasks. A sequence with one current action supports setup without requiring every decision simultaneously.

evidence.title: User details
evidence.text: The next step focuses on the profile, separate from workspace configuration.

evidence.title: Security

label: Meta Ads
title: From an account to an advertisement.
summary: Preserve the hierarchy of advertising objects while making their settings accessible.
problem: Accounts, campaigns, ad sets and statistics represent different levels of one advertising structure.
decision: Tables support list work, while an individual object’s settings open within its own context.
story: The challenge
Connect social and advertising accounts to campaigns, ad sets and individual advertisements.
Context across levels
The selected account stays on the left while the right-hand area switches between Campaigns, Adsets and Ads. Moving down the hierarchy does not require finding the account again.
Account management
Account creation opens in a dedicated form. Cards and indicators communicate selection and object state.
Working without data
Empty states distinguish missing accounts from missing rows. A loading error includes a retry action.
reasoning: Make the advertising hierarchy visible
Campaigns, ad sets and ads belong to the selected account. A persistent account area makes that relationship visible when moving between levels.
